avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction and P-glycoprotein upregulation reduces loperamide levels and efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative antidiarrheal if St. John's Wort is necessary

avoid_supplements.name: Grapefruit seed extract
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases loperamide bioavailability and CNS penetration, elevating toxicity risk
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue grapefruit products; allow 48-72 hours washout before loperamide use

caution_supplements.name: Quercetin
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential CYP3A4 inhibition may modestly increase loperamide levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for increased side effects (constipation, dizziness); dose adjustment rarely needed

caution_supplements.name: Goldenseal
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild CYP3A4 inhibition may increase loperamide exposure
caution_supplements.action: Use with caution; monitor for anticholinergic effects

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition significantly increases loperamide absorption and CNS levels, risking QT prolongation and opioid toxicity
avoid_foods.action: Avoid grapefruit products entirely during loperamide therapy

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May increase loperamide absorption and delay gastric emptying, potentially prolonging drug effect
caution_foods.action: Take loperamide consistently with or without food for predictable efficacy

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing foods/beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine may counteract loperamide's constipating effects but carries no direct pharmacokinetic interaction
caution_foods.action: Counsel patient that caffeine may reduce efficacy; monitor symptom control

monitoring_notes: Loperamide has significant P-glycoprotein substrate activity; inhibitors (ketoconazole, erythromycin, verapamil) can dramatically increase CNS exposure and toxicity risk. Monitor for signs of opioid overdose (respiratory depression, altered mental status, QT prolongation) especially when combined with CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors, even at standard doses.
